p.src: Now Yan Qing, though ranked last among the Thirty-six Stars, was quick-witted and ingenious, widely experienced and knowledgeable, and understood both himself and his destiny better than any of the other thirty-five. That day Yan Qing reported to Song Jiang, “Ever since childhood, I, Little Yi, have followed Squire Lu and learned these wrestling skills, and I have never yet met my match in the martial world. Now that this fortunate opportunity has arisen and the twenty-eighth day of the third month is near, I need not take a single man with me. I shall go alone to the challenge platform and, come what may, grapple with him for a bout. If I lose and die, I shall bear no resentment forevermore; but if by chance I win, it will add a little luster to you, elder brother. There is certain to be a fine commotion that day, so please send men to support me.” Song Jiang said, “Brother, I hear that man stands ten feet tall, looks like a guardian deity, and possesses the strength of a thousand catties or more. With such a slight and slender frame, how can you get close enough to him, however skilled you may be?” Yan Qing replied, “I do not fear his great size; I fear only that he may not fall into my trap. As the saying goes, ‘In wrestling, the strong use strength, while the weak contend with wit.’ It is not that I, Yan Qing, mean to boast, but by adapting to circumstances and acting as the moment demands, I shall not necessarily lose to that lumbering fool.” Lu Junyi then said, “My Little Yi truly has practiced excellent wrestling since childhood. Let him do as he wishes and go. When the day comes, I shall go in person to support him and bring him back.” Song Jiang asked, “When can you set out?” Yan Qing answered, “Today is already the twenty-fourth day of the third month. Tomorrow I shall bid you farewell and descend the mountain, spend a night or so on the road, reach the temple on the twenty-sixth, spend the twenty-seventh making inquiries there, and on the twenty-eighth face that fellow in combat.” Nothing further happened that day.

p.src: The next day, Song Jiang laid out wine to see Yan Qing off. When the company looked at Yan Qing, they saw that he was dressed in the plainest rustic fashion, his embroidered body hidden beneath a padded jacket. Disguised as a Shandong peddler, he had a small pellet drum tucked into his belt and carried a tall-shouldered pole laden with assorted wares; everyone laughed at the sight. Song Jiang said, “Since you are disguised as a peddler with his wares, sing us a Shandong peddler’s modulated song.” Yan Qing twirled the pellet drum with one hand and beat time with clappers in the other, then sang the peddler’s song of peace in a manner indistinguishable from a native of Shandong, making everyone laugh again. When the wine had brought them to half-drunkenness, Yan Qing took leave of all the chieftains and descended the mountain. After crossing Golden Sands Beach, he took the road toward Tai’an Prefecture.

p.src: As evening fell that day and he was just about to seek an inn for the night, he heard someone call from behind, “Brother Yan Little Yi, wait for me!” Yan Qing set down his load and looked. It was Li Kui, the Black Whirlwind. Yan Qing said, “Why have you come chasing after me?” Li Kui replied, “You accompanied me on two journeys to Jingmen Town. When I saw you setting out alone, I could not rest easy. Without telling our elder brother, I slipped down from the mountain and came especially to help you.” Yan Qing said, “I have no use for you here. Go back at once.” Li Kui flared up and said, “Even if you truly are a formidable hero, I came with good intentions to help you, yet you twist them into ill intent! Well, I am going whether you like it or not!” Yan Qing reflected that refusing him might damage their brotherly bond, so he said to Li Kui, “I do not mind taking you with me. But it is the Holy Emperor’s birthday there, and people from every mountain and region will gather. Many of them know you. If you agree to three conditions of mine, I shall let you come.” Li Kui said, “I agree.” Yan Qing said, “From now on, while we are on the road, you and I must walk separately, one ahead and one behind. The moment we reach an inn, once you enter its door, you must not come out again. That is the first condition. Second, once we reach the inn by the temple, you must pretend to be ill, wrap the quilt around your head and face, feign sleep with loud snores, and make no sound besides. Third, on the day of the temple festival, when you squeeze among the crowd to watch the wrestling, you must not make a startled fuss over anything. Elder brother, can you abide by that?” Li Kui replied, “What is difficult about that? I shall do everything you say.” That night, the two lodged at an inn.

p.src: The next day, they rose at the fifth watch, paid for their room, and went on together until they stopped farther ahead to kindle a fire and eat. Yan Qing said, “Brother Li, walk half a li ahead. I shall follow behind.” On that road, worshippers came and went without cease. Many were discussing Ren Yuan’s prowess, saying that he had gone unmatched at Mount Tai for two years and that another three years had now passed. Yan Qing took what he heard to heart. As the hour of the Monkey approached, the crowd beside the temple all stopped and stood gazing upward. Yan Qing set down his load, pushed through the crowd, and edged forward to look. He saw two red banner posts much like the signboard frame over the entrance to a neighborhood lane, supporting a white placard that read: “Taiyuan Wrestler ‘Pillar That Props Up Heaven’ Ren Yuan.” Two smaller lines at the side read: “With his fists he strikes the fierce tiger of the Southern Mountains; with his feet he kicks the blue dragon of the Northern Sea.” After reading it, Yan Qing snatched up his carrying pole and smashed the placard to pieces. Without saying a word, he shouldered his load again and went toward the temple. Among the onlookers were many meddlers, and they hurried to report to Ren Yuan that someone had broken his placard and challenged him that year.

p.src: Meanwhile, Yan Qing met Li Kui farther ahead, and the two went to seek an inn where they could rest. The area around the temple was extraordinarily bustling. Quite apart from merchants and traders of all the hundred and twenty trades, there were as many as fourteen or fifteen hundred inns receiving pilgrims from across the realm. When the sacred festival of the deity arrived, there was nowhere left to accommodate people, and the many inns were all filled to capacity. Yan Qing and Li Kui had no choice but to rent a room in an inn at the edge of the market. They set down the load, obtained a lined quilt, and Yan Qing told Li Kui to lie down beneath it. The inn servant came and asked, “Elder brother, you are a Shandong peddler who has come to do business at the temple fair. You would not happen to be unable to afford the room, would you?” Speaking in a rustic accent, Yan Qing replied, “How you look down on people! How much can one small room be worth? Even if you charge me the price of a large room, I have nowhere else to stay. Whatever others pay for their rooms, I shall pay you the same.” The inn servant said, “Do not take offense, elder brother. These are the busiest days, so it is best to make things clear beforehand.” Yan Qing said, “I have always traveled about doing business, so I myself am not a concern—I can lodge anywhere. But unexpectedly I met this kinsman from my home district on the road, and he is now suffering from a respiratory illness. That is why I had no choice but to ask for lodging at your inn. I shall give you five strings of copper cash now. Please arrange some tea and food for me from your kitchen, and when I depart I shall reward you further all at once.” The young servant accepted the copper cash and went out front to arrange the tea and food; there is no need to dwell on it.

p.src: Before long, a commotion arose outside the inn. Twenty or thirty burly men came in and asked the waiter, “In which room is the hero who split the placard and challenged the champion lodging?” The waiter said, “There is no such man here.” The men said, “Everyone says he is staying at your inn.” The waiter said, “We have only two rooms. One is empty, and the other has been rented by a Shandong peddler who is looking after a sick man.” The men said, “That peddler is the very man who split the placard and issued the challenge.” The waiter said, “Do not let others make a fool of you! That peddler is only a slight young fellow. What could he possibly do?” They all said, “Just take us to have a look.” The waiter pointed and said, “It is the room over there in the corner.” When the men went to look, they found the door tightly shut. Peering through a chink in the window, they saw two men asleep on the bed with their feet pressed against each other. They could make nothing of it. One among them said, “If he has dared to split the placard and seeks to contend with the best under Heaven, he cannot be an ordinary man. He must fear that someone will plot against him, so he is surely only pretending to be ill.” The others said, “That must be it. There is no use guessing; we shall see when the time comes.” By dusk, no fewer than twenty or thirty parties had come to the inn making inquiries, and the waiter talked until his lips were sore from explaining. That evening, when the waiter brought food for the two men, Li Kui poked his head out from beneath the covers. The waiter started at the sight and cried, “Ah! This is the gentleman who is going to wrestle!” Yan Qing said, “He is not the wrestler. He is ill; I am the one who has come expressly to compete.” The waiter said, “Do not try to deceive me. To my eyes, Ren Yuan could swallow you whole.” Yan Qing said, “Do not laugh at me. I have my own method. I shall give you all occasion for a hearty laugh, and when I return I will reward you generously with some of the prizes.” The waiter watched them finish supper, cleared away the bowls and plates, and went back to the kitchen to wash them, still unable to believe a word of it.

p.src: The temple stands upon mighty Mount Tai, the mountain that anchors Heaven and Earth. Supreme among all mountains and peaks, it is the seat of the sovereign of the myriad gods. Leaning upon a railing at the summit, one may gaze straight toward the Weak Water and Penglai; Climbing among the pines on the highest crest, one finds only dense clouds and thin mist. The towers rise thick and high, as though the golden sun-crow had flown down with wings outspread; The tiered halls soar aloft, as though the jade hare had bounded here from the moon. Carved beams and painted rafters stand beneath green tiles and vermilion eaves. Phoenix-carved doors gleam against yellow gauze, while tortoiseshell-patterned embroidered curtains trail brocade ribbons. Seen from afar, the sacred image wears a crown with nine pendants and bears the eyes of Shun and the brows of Yao; Viewed close at hand, the god's august form in its dragon-embroidered imperial robe has the shoulders of Tang and the back of Yu. The Arbiter of Fate of the Ninth Heaven wears a lotus crown that sets off his crimson gauze robe; The Holy Lord Bingling is splendidly suited by a blue-jade belt over his reddish-yellow robe. The attendants on the left wear jade hairpins and pearl-studded shoes; those on the right bear purple ribbons and golden seals. The whole hall is stern and majestic, guarded by three thousand generals in golden armor; The two galleries bristle with valor, as a hundred thousand iron-clad soldiers serve their sovereign. The Tower of the Five Peaks adjoins the Eastern Palace, while the Hall of Benevolent Peace stands close beside the Northern Gate. Below Mount Haoli, the judges divide the work of the seventy-two bureaus; Within the Temple of the White Mule, the local gods regulate the twenty-four seasonal divisions. The iron-faced Grand Commandant who governs the Pool of Fire reveals his divine power month after month; The General of the Five Paths who commands life and death manifests his holiness year after year. Imperial incense burns without cease, while heavenly spirits gallop forth to report the vermilion writs; Sacrifices are offered at their appointed times, and old and young alike receive blessings when they hear of the god's renown. Auspicious clouds veil the Hall of Jianing, and fortunate vapors coil about the Gate of Zhengyang. Ten thousand people worship the Lady of the Azure Clouds, and folk from the four quarters put their faith in the Benevolent and Sagely Emperor.

p.src: After Yan Qing had made a tour of the place, he went out to the Caocan Pavilion, bowed four times, and asked one of the incense burners, “Where is Wrestling Instructor Ren lodging?” An eager onlooker replied, “He is at the large inn below Ying'en Bridge. He has two or three hundred accomplished disciples under his instruction.” Hearing this, Yan Qing went straight to Ying'en Bridge. There he saw twenty or thirty wrestling disciples seated on the railings beside the bridge. Before them stood gilded banners and placards, brocade valances, and full-length backrests. Yan Qing slipped into the inn and saw Ren Yuan seated in the middle of a pavilion. Truly, he had the bearing of a guardian deity and the features of a Vajra. With his chest laid bare, he displayed the tiger-slaying might of Cunxiao; Seated sideways on a folding stool, he possessed the mountain-uprooting power of the Hegemon-King. He was watching his disciples wrestle there. One of those present recognized Yan Qing as the man who had split the placard and secretly reported it to Ren Yuan. Ren Yuan sprang to his feet, swung his great arms, and declared, “What doomed wretch has come this year to surrender his life into my hands?” Yan Qing lowered his head and hurried out of the inn, hearing everyone inside burst into laughter. He hurried back to his lodgings, arranged some wine and food, and ate for a while with Li Kui. Li Kui said, “Lying about like this is boring me to death!” Yan Qing said, “Only one more night. Tomorrow it will be decided who is the stronger.” Their idle talk at that time need not be related.

p.src: Around the third watch, they heard a great burst of drums and music: the temple's incense officials were offering birthday congratulations to the Holy Emperor. Around the fourth watch, Yan Qing and Li Kui rose. They first asked the waiter for hot water and washed their faces, then combed their hair smooth. They took off the padded jackets worn beneath their clothes, tightly bound their calves and fastened knee guards, hitched up soft-silk wrestling breeches, put on many-eared hemp shoes, and over their undershirts donned shoulder sashes and belted their waists. After the two had eaten breakfast, they called the waiter and instructed him, “Take good care of the baggage in our room.” The waiter replied, “Nothing will go missing. Return early and victorious.” Even in this small inn there were twenty or thirty pilgrims burning incense. They all said to Yan Qing, “Young man, consider this carefully and do not throw your life away for nothing.” Yan Qing said, “When I call for cheers, I ask you all to help me seize some of the prizes.” Some among them had already gone on ahead. Li Kui said, “It would be well if I took these two axes along.” Yan Qing said, “That will never do. If people see through our disguise, the great affair will be ruined.” The two then mingled with the crowd, went ahead to the gallery, and concealed themselves there together.

p.src: The incense-burning crowds that day truly stood shoulder to shoulder and back against back. The vast Temple of the Eastern Peak filled in a single surge, and even its roof ridges were covered with spectators. Facing the Hall of Jianing, a lofty festival scaffold had been erected, laden with gold and silver vessels and bolts of embroidered silk; Outside the gate stood five fine horses tethered, each fully saddled and bridled. The prefect ordered the pilgrims held back so that they might watch that year's wrestling offered to the Holy Emperor. An elderly military officer, bamboo tally in hand, mounted the presentation platform. After paying his respects to the god, he invited this year's wrestling challengers to come forth and contend.

u.src: The incense-burning crowds that day truly stood shoulder to shoulder and back against back. The vast Temple of the Eastern Peak filled in a single surge, and even its roof ridges were covered with spectators.
Facing the Hall of Jianing, a lofty festival scaffold had been erected, laden with gold and silver vessels and bolts of embroidered silk;
Outside the gate stood five fine horses tethered, each fully saddled and bridled.

p.src: Before he had finished speaking, the crowd surged like a tide, and more than a dozen pairs of men bearing quarterstaffs came forward, preceded by four embroidered banners. Ren Yuan sat in a sedan chair, with twenty or thirty pairs of tattooed stalwarts crowding before and behind it, and thus arrived at the presentation platform. The marshal invited him to descend from the chair and offered a few cordial words of greeting. Ren Yuan said, “For the past two years I have come to Mount Tai, taken first prize, and carried off a great quantity of rewards for nothing. This year I shall certainly have to strip for the bout.” When he had finished, a man carrying a bucket of water came forward. Ren Yuan’s disciples stood densely packed all around the edge of the presentation platform. Ren Yuan first bared his arms and removed his headcloth, leaving his Sichuan-brocade jacket loosely draped about him. He shouted a salutation to the god, received two mouthfuls of holy water, and cast off the brocade jacket, whereupon the vast crowd roared its acclaim as one. And how was Ren Yuan arrayed when one looked upon him?

p.src: His hair was bound in a coiled knot with a red horn-shaped pin thrust through its heart; about his waist he wore a crimson gauze belt with green streamers in three strands, fastened by twelve jade butterfly clasps, while over his waistcoat lay a pleated undershirt adorned with rows of golden mandarin ducks. Within his kneeguards were copper crotch plates and copper fittings; inside his leggings were iron plates and iron rings. His wrist guards were firmly bound, his kicking shoes tightly fastened. A pillar that could uphold heaven and bestride the seas; a champion beneath the sacred mountain who subdued demons and struck down generals.

p.src: The marshal said, “For two years, Master, you have met no opponent at the temple, and this is now your third contest. What words have you for all the pilgrims under heaven?” Ren Yuan said, “From four hundred prefectures and more than seven thousand counties, worthy pilgrims who revere the Holy Emperor have all contributed prizes, and for two years I, Ren Yuan, have received them without earning them. This year I shall take leave of the Holy Emperor and return home, never to climb this mountain again. From where the sun rises in the east to where it sets in the west, beneath the twin wheels of sun and moon and throughout the united realm of heaven and earth—from the southern barbarians to You and Yan in the north—is there anyone who dares come forth and contend with me for the prizes?”

p.src: Before he had finished speaking, Yan Qing pressed down upon the shoulders and arms of the men to either side and cried, “Here! Here!” He flew straight over the people’s backs and sprang onto the presentation platform. The whole crowd raised a shout. The marshal received him and asked, “Fellow, what is your surname and given name? Where are you from? And whence have you come?” Yan Qing replied, “I am Zhang the peddler from Shandong, and I have come expressly to contend with him for the prizes.” The marshal said, “Fellow, your life may be lost before your eyes. Do you understand that? Do you have a guarantor?” Yan Qing replied, “I am my own guarantor. If I die, whose life would I ask in payment?” The marshal said, “Then strip and let us look at you.” Yan Qing removed his headcloth, revealing two neatly combed horn-shaped tufts. He took off his straw sandals and bared his feet, crouched at one side of the presentation platform, and undid his leg bindings and kneeguards. Then he sprang up, stripped off his cloth shirt, and struck a pose. At once the spectators in the temple seemed like churning seas and overturning rivers, roaring wave upon wave of applause, until everyone stood amazed. When Ren Yuan saw his splendid tattoos and lithe, vigorous body, fear entered his heart by half.

p.src: Outside the palace gate, the prefect of the district sat on the raised terrace keeping order, with seventy or eighty pairs of black-clad clerks and constables standing around him. He at once sent someone to summon Yan Qing down from the presentation platform and bring him before him. Seeing the tattoos upon his body, like soft kingfisher plumage spread over a pillar of jade, the prefect was greatly delighted and asked, “Fellow, where are you from? Why have you come here?” Yan Qing replied, “My humble surname is Zhang, and I am the eldest of my family. I come from Laizhou in Shandong. Hearing that Ren Yuan had challenged all men under heaven to wrestle him, I came expressly to contest a bout with him.” The prefect said, “That fully saddled horse in front is a prize I contributed for Ren Yuan. As for all the articles upon the prize pavilion, I shall order half given to you. Divide them between you two, and I shall personally take you into my service.” Yan Qing said, “My lord, the prizes matter little. I only want to throw him, make the crowd laugh at him, and win a burst of applause.” The prefect said, “He is a great hulk of a man like a guardian deity. You will not dare come to grips with him!” Yan Qing said, “I shall have no regrets even if I die.” He returned to the presentation platform to arrange the match with Ren Yuan. The marshal first demanded the written terms; drawing the wrestling society’s rules from his robe, he read them through once. Then he said to Yan Qing, “Do you understand? No secret tricks are permitted.” Yan Qing sneered. “His whole body is protected, while I have nothing but this bare cudgel of mine. What secret trick could I play on him?” The prefect again summoned the marshal and instructed him, “Such a fine fellow, and so handsome a youth—what a pity it would be! Go and divide the prizes between them and call off the bout.” The marshal immediately returned to the presentation platform and said to Yan Qing, “Fellow, spare your life and go home. I shall settle this bout by dividing the prizes with you.” Yan Qing said, “You understand nothing! How do you know whether I shall win or lose?” The crowd all joined in the clamor. The tens of thousands of pilgrims parted and formed ranks on both sides like fish scales. Even the covered walks and rooftops were packed with seated spectators, all fearful of having their view of the wrestlers blocked. By now Ren Yuan’s heart was set: he longed to hurl Yan Qing beyond the highest clouds and dash him to death. The marshal said, “Since you two insist upon wrestling, let this pair contest this year’s bout in honor of the Holy Emperor. Both of you be careful, and each stay on your guard.” Only three men now remained upon the swept-clean presentation platform. The night dew had wholly vanished and the rising sun had just appeared. Holding his bamboo tally, the marshal finished instructing both sides, then called, “Begin the bout!”

p.src: This wrestling bout, with its advances and retreats, must be related with the utmost clarity. One may be slow in telling it, but the action itself was swift—as stars shifted and lightning flashed through the sky, allowing not the slightest delay. Yan Qing crouched in a compact ball on the right, while Ren Yuan first took his stance on the left. Yan Qing did not stir. At first each occupied half the presentation platform, their minds fixed upon the moment they would close. Seeing that Yan Qing did not move, Ren Yuan gradually pressed toward the right, while Yan Qing kept watching only the lower part of his body. Ren Yuan thought to himself, “This fellow is surely planning some trick against my lower body. Watch me! I need not even use my hands; with one kick I shall send the rogue off the platform.” As Ren Yuan edged closer, he feigned an opening with his left leg. Yan Qing cried, “Stay back!” Just as Ren Yuan was about to rush him, Yan Qing slipped beneath Ren Yuan’s left ribs and darted past. Enraged, Ren Yuan wheeled around and reached for Yan Qing again, but Yan Qing made a feinting leap and slipped beneath his right ribs this time. Turning was awkward for so huge a man, and after three such changes his footwork fell into disorder. Yan Qing darted in, gripped Ren Yuan with his right hand, thrust his left hand between Ren Yuan’s thighs, and braced his shoulder blade against the man’s chest. He hoisted Ren Yuan straight into the air, head heavy and feet light, then used the momentum to whirl him four or five times. Spinning to the edge of the presentation platform, he shouted, “Down you go!” Then he hurled Ren Yuan straight off the presentation platform, head downward and feet in the air. This throw was called the “Pigeon Whirl.” When the tens of thousands of pilgrims saw it, they cheered with one voice!

p.src: Among the temple attendants were some who recognized Li Kui, and they called out his name. The constables outside all rushed into the temple, shouting, “Don’t let the ‘Black Whirlwind’ of Liangshan Marsh escape!” When the prefect heard this, his three souls seemed to fly from the crown of his head and his seven spirits to scatter beneath his feet; he fled at once toward the rear hall. People surged in from every side to surround them, while the temple attendants scattered in flight. Li Kui looked at Ren Yuan and saw him lying unconscious beside the offering platform, with only the faintest breath left in his mouth. Li Kui tore up a stone slab and smashed Ren Yuan’s head to pulp. The two fought their way out of the temple, but arrows came flying thickly through the doorway. Yan Qing and Li Kui had no choice but to scramble onto the roof, tear up the tiles, and hurl them wildly below.

p.src: Before long, a tremendous battle cry arose before the temple gate, and men came fighting their way inside. At their head came a man wearing a white Fanyang felt hat and a white satin jacket, with a saber at his waist and a long-handled blade leveled before him. He was Lu Junyi, the “Jade Qilin” of Beijing. Behind him came the seven heroes Shi Jin, Mu Hong, Lu Zhishen, Wu Song, Xie Zhen, and Xie Bao, leading over a thousand men. They forced open the temple gate and entered to support their comrades. When Yan Qing and Li Kui saw them, they leaped down from the roof and withdrew with the main force. Li Kui ran to the inn to fetch his twin axes, then hurried back to join the fighting. By the time the prefecture had mustered and counted its troops, the band of heroes was already far away. Knowing that the forces of Liangshan Marsh were too formidable to oppose, the government troops dared not pursue them.

We must send someone to find him and bring him back to the mountain.” Mu Hong said, “I’ll find him and bring him back to the stronghold.” “Excellent,” said Lu Junyi.

p.src: Leaving Lu Junyi to lead the others back to the mountain, let us speak instead of Li Kui, who went straight to Shouzhang County with his twin axes in hand. The midday court session had just ended when Li Kui reached the county yamen gate and strode in, roaring, “Your father, the ‘Black Whirlwind’ of Liangshan Marsh, is here!” Everyone in the yamen was so terrified that their limbs went numb and they could not move. Shouzhang County lay closer to Liangshan Marsh than any other. The mere five words “Black Whirlwind Li Kui” were truly enough to cure a child of crying in fright at night; now that he had come in person, how could they not be afraid?

p.src: Li Kui went straight to the magistrate’s chair and sat down, shouting, “Send two men out to speak with me! If no one comes, I’ll set the place on fire!” The men in the rooms off the corridor consulted together. “We can only send a few men out to answer him. Otherwise, how shall we ever make him leave?” Two clerks among them came into the hall, bowed four times, and knelt, saying, “Our chief has surely come here with some command for us.” Li Kui said, “I haven’t come to trouble the people of your county. I was passing this way and thought I’d amuse myself awhile. Invite your magistrate out so that I may meet him.” The two men went away, then returned to report, “When His Honor the magistrate saw our chief arrive just now, he opened the rear gate and fled. We do not know where he has gone.” Li Kui did not believe them and went into the rear chambers to search for himself. “Chief, look—his chest of clothes is still sitting over there.” Li Kui twisted the lock open, took out an official cap, spread its winged corners and put it on, then donned the green official robe and fastened the horn belt around his waist; then he found a pair of black official boots and exchanged his hemp sandals for them. Holding an official tablet, he strode into the front hall and shouted, “Let all clerks and functionaries come pay their respects!” The men had no choice but to go forward and obey. Li Kui asked, “Do I look good dressed like this?” “It suits you perfectly,” they replied. Li Kui said, “Bring all your secretaries and attendants here to hold court for me, and then I will go; but if you disobey me, I’ll raze this whole county to bare ground.” Afraid of him, they had to assemble some of the yamen staff. The men held ceremonial staves and maces, sounded three rolls on the court drum, and came forward to salute him. Li Kui laughed heartily, then said, “Have two of your men come forward with a lawsuit as well.” A clerk said, “With our chief sitting here, who would dare come and lodge a complaint?” Li Kui said, “Of course no one will come to lodge a complaint. Choose two men yourselves and have them pretend to bring a case before me. I won’t hurt them. I only want a little amusement and laughter.” After consulting for a while, the yamen staff had no choice but to make two jailers pretend they had fought and come forward with their complaints. The common people outside the county gate were all admitted to watch. The two knelt before the hall, and one complained, “Your Honor, have mercy! He struck this humble man.” The other said, “He insulted this humble man, so I struck him.” Li Kui asked, “Which of you was beaten?” The plaintiff said, “This humble man was the one beaten.” He asked again, “Which of you struck him?” The defendant said, “He insulted me first. This humble man did indeed strike him.” Li Kui said, “The man who struck another is a true hero. Release him at once. As for this worthless fellow, how could he let someone beat him? Put him in a cangue and display him before the yamen.” Li Kui rose, tucked up the green robe, thrust the official tablet into his belt, and drew a great ax. He stayed to watch until the plaintiff had been put in the cangue and displayed before the county yamen; only then did he stride away, still wearing the official robe and boots. The common people watching before the yamen gate could no longer contain their laughter.

p.src: Li Kui was wandering east and west before the Shouzhang county yamen when he suddenly heard the sound of reading from a school. He lifted the curtain and went inside, frightening the teacher into leaping through a window and fleeing. Among the pupils, some cried, some screamed, some ran, and some hid. Li Kui laughed loudly and came back out, only to run straight into Mu Hong. Mu Hong cried, “Everyone has been worried sick over you, yet here you are running wild! Hurry back up the mountain!” He gave Li Kui no say in the matter, but seized him and dragged him away. Li Kui had no choice but to leave Shouzhang County and head straight back to Liangshan Marsh. A poem bears witness:

u.src: Li Kui was wandering east and west before the Shouzhang county yamen when he suddenly heard the sound of reading from a school. He lifted the curtain and went inside, frightening the teacher into leaping through a window and fleeing.
Among the pupils, some cried, some screamed, some ran, and some hid.
Li Kui laughed loudly and came back out, only to run straight into Mu Hong.
Mu Hong cried, “Everyone has been worried sick over you, yet here you are running wild!
Hurry back up the mountain!”
He gave Li Kui no say in the matter, but seized him and dragged him away.
Li Kui had no choice but to leave Shouzhang County and head straight back to Liangshan Marsh.
A poem bears witness:

p.src: Magistrates charged to tend the people often act like tyrants; their teachers must have taught them poorly from childhood. Iron Ox should be sent to make his rounds, creating an uproar in the court and then another in the school.

p.src: The two crossed Golden Sands Beach and returned to the stronghold. Everyone laughed when they saw Li Kui dressed in such fashion. When they reached the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness, Song Jiang was celebrating with Yan Qing. Li Kui set down the skirts of his green robe, removed his twin axes, and swaggered straight to the front of the hall. Holding the official tablet, he began to bow before Song Jiang. Before he had completed two bows, he stepped on the green robe and tore it, tripping himself and falling to the floor. Everyone laughed. Song Jiang cursed him. “You scoundrel, you are far too audacious! You slipped down the mountain without informing me. That is a crime deserving death! Wherever you go, you stir up trouble. I tell you now before all our brothers: next time I will not spare you!” Li Kui repeatedly murmured his assent and withdrew.

p.src: From then on, the men and horses of Liangshan Marsh remained safe and nothing much occurred. Each day, martial skills were taught and practiced in the stronghold, the troops and horses were drilled, and those who knew the water were ordered aboard boats to train. In every stockade they also made additional weapons, robes, armor, spears and sabers, bows and arrows, shields and crossbows, and banners; but of this there is no need to speak further.

p.src: Now the military commander of Tai'an Prefecture reported the preceding events to the Eastern Capital. The Memorials Office had also received petitions from prefectures and counties throughout the realm, all reporting that Song Jiang and his followers were in rebellion and disturbing the countryside. At this time, the Daojun Emperor had not held court or attended to affairs of state for a full month. When the morning audience was held that day, three cracks of the ceremonial whip rang before the imperial palace, and the two ranks of civil and military officials took their places upon the golden steps. The master of ceremonies called out, “Those with matters to report, step forward and speak at once; if there is no business, let the curtain be rolled up and the court dismissed.” The director of the Memorials Office stepped from the ranks and reported, “My office has repeatedly received petitions from prefectures and counties everywhere, all stating that Song Jiang and his bandits openly march straight into prefectural cities, plunder treasuries, raid granaries, and slaughter soldiers and civilians. Their greed knows no bounds, and wherever they go, no one can withstand them. Unless they are suppressed and captured without delay, they are certain to become a grave menace in time.” The Son of Heaven said, “These brigands caused an uproar in the capital on the night of the Lantern Festival, and now they are disturbing every region. What, then, must it be like in the prefectures and commanderies near their lair? I have repeatedly ordered the Bureau of Military Affairs to dispatch troops, yet to this day no report has returned.” Then Censor-in-Chief Cui Jing, who stood nearby, stepped from the ranks and reported, “I have heard that a great banner has been raised at Liangshan Marsh, bearing the four characters ‘Carry Out Justice on Heaven’s Behalf.’ This is a means of winning over the people. Since the people’s hearts have already turned toward them, troops should not be sent against them. At present the Liao armies are invading our borders, and our forces in every quarter can scarcely hold them back. It would therefore be highly inconvenient to raise another army for a punitive campaign. In my humble opinion, these desperate men of the hills have all broken the law and, having nowhere to escape, gathered in bands among the mountains and forests, where they have given themselves over to lawlessness. If Your Majesty were to issue a vermilion edict, have the Court of Imperial Entertainments provide imperial wine and delicacies, and send a high minister directly to Liangshan Marsh to soothe and admonish them with kindly words, they might accept amnesty and submit. They could then be used to oppose the Liao forces, benefiting both the state and the people. I humbly beg Your Majesty to judge the matter with your sacred wisdom.” The Son of Heaven said, “Your words are most fitting and accord perfectly with my own wishes.” He thereupon appointed Palace Commandant Chen Zongshan as his envoy and ordered him to bear the vermilion edict and imperial wine to Liangshan Marsh, there to offer amnesty to all its people, high and low.

p.src: That same day, Grand Commandant Chen received the imperial edict at court and returned home to make ready. Yet Grand Commandant Chen’s mission under imperial command to offer amnesty was destined to turn fragrant wine into a potion that scorched the body, and the vermilion edict into a summons to battle. How Grand Commandant Chen went about offering amnesty to Song Jiang will be revealed in the next chapter.
